item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Field Service - Preserve actual booking End Time when completion is recorded later
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to Preserve actual booking End Time when completion is recorded later in Dynamics 365 Field Service. This feature will reach public preview on November 22, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature allows Field Service administrators to choose whether completion by the booked resource automatically changes the booking End Time. Admins complete bookings later can preserve the existing or explicitly supplied work end, helping booking duration and downstream time and cost records remain aligned with when the work occurred.

Use the organization-level Set End Time on booked resource completion setting in Field Service settings to control the automatic End Time update.
  • With the setting set to Yes, which is the default, current behavior is preserved. When the booked resource completes a booking without supplying End Time, Field Service sets End Time to the completion time and recalculates Duration.
  • With the setting set to No, Field Service preserves End Time and Duration when the booked resource completes the booking unless the completion request explicitly supplies a different End Time.
  • Completion by another user or an integration continues to preserve End Time for either setting value.
  • When the setting is No and the booked resource completes the booking, Field Service uses the retained or supplied End Time as the effective Completed booking timestamp. This keeps timestamp-derived booking journals and automatic time entries aligned with the recorded work end. Dataverse audit fields continue to show when the completion was submitted.
The setting applies to future completion transitions and does not rewrite historical bookings. It does not change the booking-status lifecycle, invoice generation, or the existing Work Order Completed On calculation, which continues to use the latest eligible booking End Time.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [stayInformed] Copilot Studio - Credit visibility in run view & monitor in workflows
item.description:
We are announcing Copilot Credit visibility in run view and monitors in workflows in Copilot Studio. This feature reached general availability on November 11, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Makers will now be able to see how many Copilot Credits each workflow run consumes directly from the workflow designer. This allows makers to predict and control the cost of automation before scaling it to production, and to quickly identify which steps are driving consumption.

This feature brings the following improvements:
  • Run Details: A credits pill shows the estimated credits per run and per step.
  • Monitor tab: You can now view credits used across runs to understand and predict costs.
  • Capacity awareness: A warning banner will appear when credit limits are approaching or have been reached, and test runs will be blocked when credits are exhausted.
What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [planForChange] Release Planner Retirement: D365, Power Platform, and Dataverse Move to AI at Work
item.description:
Release Planner is now retired. To stay informed about upcoming capabilities and prepare your organization for feature rollout and adoption, use the resources shared below. To view product availability for Dynamics 365, Power Platform and Copilot Studio, visit the new Learn page at https://aka.ms/d365-product-availability.


Starting this fall, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Dataverse roadmap content is joining the AI at Work roadmap, giving customers a single destination to discover upcoming capabilities, track rollout progress, and plan adoption across Microsoft's business applications, productivity, and AI portfolio.

As part of this transition, Release Planner will retire on November 15, 2026. Microsoft is also retiring the twice-yearly release wave communication model in favor of continuous roadmap disclosure and change communications. New capabilities will be published to the AI at Work roadmap as they become committed and ready to share, providing a more current and comprehensive view of upcoming innovation.

When this will happen
  • September 2026: New Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Dataverse roadmap items begin publishing directly to the AI at Work roadmap.
  • Fall 2026: Existing roadmap items with Public Preview or General Availability dates on or after June 1, 2026 transition from Release Planner to the AI at Work roadmap.
  • By November 15, 2026: Release Planner retires. The AI at Work roadmap becomes Microsoft's primary destination for public roadmap information.
How this affects your organization

If your organization uses Release Planner, Release Plans on Microsoft Learn, or release wave announcements for roadmap planning, you will need to transition to the AI at Work roadmap.

Key changes include:

  • Release Planner will retire on November 15, 2026.
  • New Release Plans will no longer be published on Microsoft Learn beginning in September 2026. Existing Release Plans will remain available for historical reference.
  • The September 2026 Release Wave 2 announcement will not occur because release wave communications are being retired.
  • Roadmap information will be published continuously rather than grouped into twice-yearly release wave announcements.
  • Roadmap content will be available through filtering, CSV export, RSS subscriptions, and the Release Communications MCP Server pulls roadmap information directly into your own AI tools and workflows.
  • Personalized saved views from My Release Plans will not migrate to the AI at Work roadmap.
What is not changing

This transition changes how Microsoft communicates roadmap information. It does not change how products are built, released, or deployed.

The following remain unchanged:

  • Product release schedules
  • Deployment and rollout processes
  • Upgrade planning and support lifecycles
  • Preview and testing programs
  • Message Center notifications, which remain the authoritative source for tenant-specific communications
  • Microsoft Learn as the home for product documentation and implementation guidance
What you can do to prepare
  • In September, begin using the AI at Work roadmap as your primary destination for roadmap planning.
  • Review internal processes, documentation, bookmarks, and communications that currently reference Release Planner, Release Plans, or release wave announcements.
  • Configure roadmap filters, RSS subscriptions, and CSV exports to support your organization's planning processes.
  • Evaluate the Release Communications MCP Server if your organization integrates roadmap data into planning workflows or AI tools.
  • Continue using Message Center for tenant-specific change notifications and deployment communications.
Additional information

The AI at Work roadmap provides a single destination for roadmap information across Microsoft business applications, productivity experiences, Copilot, agents, and AI solutions. Organizations are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the roadmap's filtering, export, RSS, and MCP capabilities before September 2026 publishing begins.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Purview: Adaptive scopes add lifecycle status evaluation controls for recipients and site owners
item.description:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Purview is introducing lifecycle status evaluation controls for adaptive scopes. This update gives administrators explicit control over whether active, inactive, and soft-deleted recipients and site owners are included in adaptive scope membership.

With this change, newly created adaptive scopes will evaluate only active recipients and site owners by default. Administrators can configure adaptive scopes to include inactive and/or soft-deleted recipients and site owners when needed.

This update also adds support for ISO 8601 duration values for selected date attributes in the adaptive scope advanced query builder.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568785.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: Beginning in December 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete in December 2026 (previously early October)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in April 2027 (previously mid-October 2026) and expected to complete in April 2027 (previously mid-November 2026)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Purview administrators who create or manage adaptive scopes.
  • Organizations that use adaptive scopes for Microsoft Purview policy targeting.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Adaptive Scopes

What will happen

Existing adaptive scopes will continue to function as they do today and will not be automatically modified as part of this rollout.

For newly created adaptive scopes:

  • Active recipients and site owners will be evaluated by default.
  • Inactive and soft-deleted recipients or site owners will not be included unless explicitly configured by an administrator.

Administrators will also have the option to update existing adaptive scopes to use explicit lifecycle status evaluation criteria for recipients and site owners.

Additionally, adaptive scopes will support ISO 8601 duration values for certain date-based attributes in the advanced query builder.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required before rollout.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review current adaptive scope configurations and governance requirements.
  • Determine whether inactive or soft-deleted recipients and site owners should be included in future adaptive scope definitions.
  • Update adaptive scope creation processes and documentation, if applicable, to account for the new lifecycle status settings.

Learn more

  • (to be updated closer to general availability): Adaptive scopes | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations have been identified.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Pages and Notebooks Creation in OneDrive
item.description:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We're changing where newly created Copilot Pages are stored. Going forward, Copilot Pages created in Copilot Chat, the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, and new Copilot Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive for Business instead of their current location.

This change enables organizations to manage newly created Copilot Pages using existing OneDrive for Business governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle management capabilities.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 (previously mid-August) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously late September)
  • General Availability (GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously early December)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

Users who create Copilot Pages in:

  • Copilot Chat
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot app
  • Copilot Notebooks

Microsoft 365 administrators responsible for governance, compliance, retention, and content management

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Copilot Chat
  • Copilot Notebooks
  • OneDrive for Business
  • Microsoft Purview compliance solutions

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in users' OneDrive for Business.
  • New Copilot Pages will appear alongside other OneDrive files, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents.
  • New Copilot Notebooks and artifacts created within them will appear alongside other OneDrive files, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents.
  • Existing OneDrive governance, compliance, data protection, retention, lifecycle management, reporting, and investigation capabilities will apply to newly created Copilot Pages.

In addition to all existing governance and management capabilities, the following additional OneDrive for Business capabilities will apply to newly created Copilot Pages:

Compliance and legal

  • Standard file path-based eDiscovery
  • Retention labels with record locking
  • Information Barriers
  • Compliance Boundaries

Data protection

  • Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and mitigation workflows
  • Third-party governance solutions that support OneDrive content

Lifecycle management

  • Retention and lifecycle policies
  • Existing departed-user workflows for OneDrive content

Monitoring and oversight

  • OneDrive storage reporting
  • Administrative investigations of content stored in OneDrive

Unaffected files

  • Existing Copilot Pages will remain in their current location and will not be migrated as part of this change.
  • Existing Copilot Notebooks will continue to store all newly created pages in SharePoint Embedded. Only Copilot Notebooks created after this change will store pages in OneDrive. 
  • Loop workspaces are not affected and will continue to use their current storage location.

IT Admin controls

  • If your organization has set Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks to Disabled, that setting will continue to be honored after this change.
  • This admin control is planned for future retirement. Microsoft will provide additional communication and transition guidance before the setting is retired.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required for the rollout.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review existing DLP, retention, and compliance policies that apply to OneDrive for Business.
  • Verify that any third-party governance or eDiscovery solutions are configured to monitor OneDrive content as appropriate.
  • Update internal documentation and governance guidance for AI-generated content.
  • Communicate to users that newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in their OneDrive for Business.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change alter where customer data is stored?Yes. Newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in OneDrive for Business instead of their previous storage location.
Does this change affect compliance and governance capabilities?Yes. Newly created Copilot Pages will be subject to OneDrive for Business compliance capabilities, including eDiscovery, retention labels with record locking, Information Barriers, and Compliance Boundaries.
Does this change affect data protection controls?Yes. Existing OneDrive for Business data protection controls, including Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and supported third-party governance solutions, can be applied to newly created Copilot Pages.
Does this change affect lifecycle management and retention processes?Yes. Existing OneDrive for Business retention policies, lifecycle management capabilities, and departed-user workflows will apply to newly created Copilot Pages.
Does this change affect how administrators monitor or investigate content?Yes. Administrators will be able to use standard OneDrive for Business reporting, monitoring, and investigation capabilities for newly created Copilot Pages.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Video sharing from OneDrive in Teams events
item.description:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the content. If you are a tenant in a GCCH or DoD environment, you can safely ignore this message as you are not impacted. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams will soon support sharing video directly from OneDrive during Teams events that are optimized for scale (previously called town halls). Organizers and producers using Manage what attendees see can load videos from OneDrive and present them on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos in PowerPoint. This improvement provides smoother, higher-quality video playback for attendees and simplifies event production through built-in video playback controls.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and end in early December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Teams event organizers and producers using events configured with Manage what attendees see.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • OneDrive
  • Teams events

What will happen

  • Organizers and producers will be able to select and share videos stored in OneDrive directly within Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see and will have access to built-in controls to start and pause video playback during events.
  • Videos can be presented on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos into a PowerPoint presentation.
  • Attendees will experience smoother and higher-quality video playback.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Inform Teams event organizers and producers that they can share videos directly from OneDrive in Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see.
  • Ensure that organizers and producers store videos in OneDrive with the appropriate permissions before using them in events.
  • Review and update internal event production guidance that recommends screen sharing locally played videos or embedding videos in PowerPoint.

We will update this post with new documentation.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Automatic recording indicator for call queue calls on Mobile
item.description:
[What and Why:]

When an organization automatically records its call queue calls, calling reps need to know at a glance that the call is being recorded and that this is controlled by the organization.

For call queue calls that are automatically recorded by the organization, Microsoft Teams on Mobile will clearly indicate that recording and transcription have started automatically and cannot be stopped. This gives calling reps a clear and accurate picture of the call and provides a consistent experience across desktop and Mobile. 

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Once available, calling reps who answer call queue calls that are automatically recorded by your organization will see the updated message in the recording banner in Teams on Mobile.

What will change:

  • The banner will state that recording started automatically and cannot be stopped.
  • The previous wording, which implied the user had started the recording, will no longer appear on these calls.

This change updates only the banner text. It applies to call queue calls that your organization records automatically. Other calls and recordings started manually by users are not affected. Existing consent text, the privacy link, and the AI notice in the banner stay the same.

This feature does not change how recordings are started, stored, or accessed. Automatic recording for call queues is already available on desktop and is configured by admins in Teams admin center. Mobile now shows the same recording state.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required before rollout. We recommend informing your calling reps about the updated banner, particularly those who answer queue calls on their mobile devices, so they know automatic recording is controlled by the organization and cannot be stopped by the rep.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Copilot in the Queues app on Mobile
item.description:
[What and Why:]

After a customer call, calling reps or supervisor leads often need to know what was discussed. They might be following up on a missed call, picking up a conversation a colleague handled, or checking how a call went. Getting those details usually means going through the call itself, which takes time, especially on Mobile.

We're introducing Copilot in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams Mobile. From shared call history, calling reps and supervisor leads can ask Copilot questions about a past call and quickly surface relevant information and insights from the conversation. This helps them get up to speed and take the next step without having to review the entire call.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid December 2026.

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on late November 2026 and expect to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Once available, eligible users will be able to use Copilot on calls in shared call history in the Queues app on Mobile.

Users will be able to:

  • Open Copilot from a recorded call in shared call history.
  • Ask questions about the call and get relevant information and insights from the conversation.
  • Understand a customer conversation and decide on a follow-up without reviewing the full call.

Copilot is available for recorded call queue calls, as it is on desktop.

 Users need a Teams Premium license to use the Queues app and a Microsoft 365 Copilot license to use Copilot.

This feature does not change how call recordings are created, stored, or accessed. Copilot in the Queues app is already available on desktop, and Mobile brings the same capability to the phone.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required before rollout.

We recommend that you:

  • Confirm that automatic recording is turned on for the call queues where you want users to use Copilot.
  • Review Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams Premium license assignments for the users who will use the feature.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Manage call groups on Mobile
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Call groups let colleagues answer calls on a user's behalf, but changing one today means going to the desktop. When availability changes, for example when a backup contact is out or a new teammate needs to cover, users often notice while they are away from their desks and cannot update their call group from the phone where they take their calls.

We're introducing the ability to create and manage a call group directly from Microsoft Teams on Mobile. Users can add or remove members, configure how the group should ring, and choose to forward or simultaneously ring incoming calls to their call group. This makes it easier for on the go users to manage how their calls are handled without needing to reach desktop.

From Settings, users can open Calling and select Manage call group to view their current call group or create a new one.

Once the call group is set up, users can forward their calls to the group or ring the group at the same time as their own devices, using the call handling options in Calling settings.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Once available, eligible users will see Manage call group in the Calling settings of Teams on Mobile.

Users will be able to:

  • View their current call group and its members.
  • Create a call group if they don't have one.
  • Add or remove members.
  • Choose how the group rings: Everyone at once or In the order below.
  • Reorder members when the ring order matters.
  • Forward calls to the call group or have the group ring alongside their own devices.

Changes made on Mobile apply to the same call group settings that users manage on desktop. Mobile adds a new way to manage them and does not introduce a separate call group.

This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license and uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups. If call groups are turned off for a user in their calling policy, they won't be able to use the feature on Mobile.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required before rollout.

Manage call groups on Mobile uses the same controls as the desktop experience.

We recommend that you:

  • Review the calling policy assigned to the users who should be able to manage call groups, and confirm that call groups are allowed.
  • Confirm that those users have a Teams Phone license.
  • Inform your users, particularly those who rely on call groups for backup coverage and often work away from their desk uses Mobile.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Workforce Intelligence plugin available in Copilot Cowork
item.description:
[What and why]

We're adding the Workforce Intelligence plugin to Microsoft Copilot Cowork and other supported plugin surfaces for tenants enrolled in Frontier. The plugin helps leaders and managers use natural language to explore their organization's structure, workforce composition, and skills, making it easier to prepare for organizational discussions and identify team-level learning opportunities.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Frontier Worldwide): Starting November 16, 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to Copilot Cowork in organizations where an admin has opted into the Frontier program, configured Workforce Insights, and made the plugin available

Note: Skills insights also require appropriate People Skills licensing and admin enablement.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft Copilot Cowork
  • Workforce Insights agent
  • Workforce Intelligence plugin
  • People Skills

What will happen

  • Explore organizational structure: Leaders and managers can ask questions about headcount, roles, functions, reporting relationships, direct reports, management layers, and locations.
  • Understand skills and learning opportunities: Users can explore collective strengths, identify opportunities for team-level learning and knowledge sharing, and assess the completeness of skills records.
  • Prepare summaries and dashboards: Users can organize workforce findings into summaries or dashboards for leadership discussions.
  • Access the plugin: Users can find the Workforce Intelligence plugin in Copilot Cowork by selecting + > Customize and searching for the plugin. Once the plugin is available and enabled, Cowork automatically selects the appropriate skill based on the conversation, so users don't need to select a skill before asking a question.
  • Existing data permissions remain unchanged: Installing the plugin does not grant additional access to workforce data. Responses depend on user permissions, connected data sources, data freshness, and admin-configured governance labels and access policies.
  • Admin configuration remains separate: Admins continue to configure organizational terminology, business context, and attribute descriptions in the Workforce Insights agent. These definitions do not modify workforce records or grant additional access.
  • Intended use and limitations: The plugin supports organizational discussions and team-level learning. It is not designed for monitoring employee behavior, managing performance, ranking employees or managers, or making employment decisions. It does not provide historical trends, forecasting, or attrition analysis.
  • Dashboard sharing: Creating a dashboard does not automatically share, publish, or schedule it for refresh.

Example prompt:

"Help me review my organization for our next leadership discussion. Focus on team sizes, management layers, locations, and opportunities for team-level learning."

[Action required and recommendations]

To prepare for this feature, admins should:

  • Verify prerequisites: Confirm that intended users have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and Cowork access, your organization has opted into the Frontier program, and Workforce Insights is configured.
  • Enable skills insights (optional): Verify appropriate People Skills licensing and enablement. 
  • Make the plugin available: Determine which leaders and managers should have access to the plugin and make it available to them. You can also optionally deploy it automatically to the intended users.
  • Review data governance: Verify access policies and governance labels to ensure users can access only permitted workforce data.
  • Configure organizational context: Define company-specific terminology and attribute descriptions in the Workforce Insights agent to help ensure responses reflect your organization's definitions.
  • Communicate with users: Explain the plugin's intended uses and limitations. Remind users that AI-generated responses may be inaccurate or incomplete and should be reviewed before sharing.

Learn more

  • Overview of People Skills | Microsoft Learn
  • Use plugins with Copilot Cowork | Microsoft Learn
  • Workforce Insights agent | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

The Workforce Intelligence plugin introduces AI-powered workforce insights through Copilot Cowork while respecting existing data access permissions and organizational governance policies.

  • The plugin uses organizational and skills data that users are authorized to access.
  • Installing the plugin does not grant additional access to workforce data or change existing access policies.
  • Admins control plugin availability and configure organizational context through Workforce Insights.
  • AI-generated workforce insights should be reviewed before sharing and should not be used for employee performance evaluation or employment decisions.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Page context for open tabs in the Copilot desktop app built-in browser
item.description:
[What and why]

Copilot in the desktop app will be able to use content from open webpage tabs in the app's built-in browser as page context. Users will be able to ask questions or request summaries for a single tab or across multiple tabs, which helps with multi-tab workflows. Page context will be scoped to the current conversation and will apply only when the built-in browser is enabled. 

Availability is limited to the Microsoft Copilot desktop app.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete the rollout in late November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of the Copilot desktop app in organizations where the built-in browser is enabled
  • Admins who manage the Copilot desktop app and its built-in browser

Platforms and services

  • Copilot desktop app (built-in browser)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • When the built-in browser is enabled, Copilot will be able to use content from open webpage tabs in that browser to answer questions and provide summaries: 

  • Users will be able to ask about a single tab or across multiple tabs: 

  • Page context will be limited to the current conversation.
  • If the built-in browser is disabled, this feature will not be active and will have no impact.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Confirm whether the Copilot desktop app built-in browser is enabled for your organization.
  • Review the governance settings for in-app browsing and page context use.
  • Validate the expected behavior with pilot users.
  • Tell users and helpdesk staff that page context is limited to the current conversation.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Copilot uses content from open webpage tabs in the built-in browser as context for answers and summaries.
Does the change give users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can ask questions or request summaries for one tab or across multiple tabs.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Suggestions to continue in another Copilot experience
item.description:

Facilitator can identify when participants ask questions or express uncertainty and retrieve and share relevant answers using web search in the meeting chat. This enhancement helps improve meeting productivity by reducing interruptions and enabling teams to stay focused on goals while accessing needed information. If a participant asks a factual question and no one responds, Facilitator can provide an answer directly in the meeting chat.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-February 2027 (previously mid-December) and expected to complete early March 2027 (previously mid-January)

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Users in Microsoft Teams meetings where Facilitator is enabled with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams (meetings)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Facilitator will monitor meeting conversations in real time to detect implicit or explicit information needs.
  • When a knowledge gap is identified, Facilitator performs a web search and posts a response in the meeting chat: 
  • Responses are infrequent in practice and typically occur less than once per meeting.
  • Responses are limited to questions relevant to the meeting discussion based on agenda signals and conversational context.
  • Facilitator must be manually added to the meeting and is not enabled by default.

  • Admins can disable Facilitator at the tenant level. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting. If web search is disabled, responses are not generated.
  • Users can stop the behavior at any time by removing Facilitator from the meeting.
  • The feature is supported in standard Teams meetings only and not supported in calls, webinars, or town halls.
  • The experience is supported in meetings that include external or cross-tenant participants.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Windows: Updates to address compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
item.description:
Updated November 11, 2026: On November 16, 2026, an update will be released for Microsoft Edge and WebView2, delivered via the PKI Metadata component, which will fully remove default trust for the remaining roots (emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA, and emSign Root TLS CA - G1). Devices check for PKI Metadata updates every 10 hours and shortly after each new app launch. 

For more information, see Microsoft Response to eMudhra Certificate Authority Key Compromise.

[What and why]

Microsoft is responding to an issue involving eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys, six associated with TLS and two with code signing. Because these keys could be recovered, they could potentially be used to create certificates or sign content that appeared to come from a trusted CA. The issue arose in eMudhra's certificate hierarchy and was not a compromise of Microsoft systems.

Microsoft is updating certificate trust to block affected certificate authorities and remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Windows, Microsoft Edge, or WebView2, particularly organizations with certificates that chain to one of the eight certificates being removed
  • Organizations managing disconnected Windows devices or disconnected Azure devices may need to take additional action

Platforms and services

  • Windows
  • Microsoft Edge
  • WebView2
  • Azure virtual machines

What will happen

  • Microsoft has published an update to the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the affected certificate authorities.
  • Microsoft has deployed a separate CRLSet update for Microsoft Edge and WebView2 to block affected TLS certificates signed by the affected certificate authorities.
  • The Microsoft Edge and WebView2 update is delivered automatically through the component update mechanism. Customers do not need to install a new browser version.
  • Microsoft has released updates to Windows and Microsoft Edge to remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies from their trust lists.
  • After these updates reach a device, the affected certificates will no longer be trusted by default through the respective trust lists.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Keep updates flowing. Allow automatic Windows certificate trust updates and Microsoft Edge component updates to reach your devices.
  • Check disconnected Windows devices. If you manage Windows devices that do not receive automatic updates, make sure your update process delivers the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and upcoming trust-list changes. See the Microsoft Learn guidance in Learn more for information about distributing certificate trust lists in disconnected environments.
  • Review disconnected Azure devices. Review disconnected Azure devices running on Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) or single-instance VMs. Updated images are available in Azure Marketplace, and customers can deploy them to protect against this vulnerability.
  • Replace dependent certificates. If any of your certificates chain to one of the seven certificates being removed, identify those dependencies and obtain replacement certificates or an alternative trusted chain before the changes reach your devices.

Learn more

  • Microsoft’s response to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
  • Configure trusted roots and disallowed certificates in Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) New Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service experiences across Teams, Copilot, and Outlook
item.description:

Microsoft is introducing new Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service experiences that bring customer context, business processes, and agent capabilities into Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Outlook, and other Microsoft 365 applications. These updates help sellers and service representatives access customer information, take actions, and collaborate without switching between applications.

  • Sales Development Agent

Platforms and services

  • Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 Apps
  • Outlook
  • Cowork
  • Code

Sales and Service Skills for Cowork, Autopilot, and Code (General Availability for Cowork, Frontier program for Code, and Private Preview for Autopilot)

Thirty sales and service skills package Dynamics 365 business expertise into reusable building blocks for Cowork, Autopilot, and Code. These skills help sellers and service representatives identify opportunities and risks, update CRM data, resolve service issues, and take actions grounded in customer data and business processes. Organizations can also use these skills with custom agents to support workflows enterprises build themselves. Learn more about the Sales and Service skills.

Dynamics 365 CRM in the flow of Teams (Public Preview)

It is managed in Teams, sends email from its own Exchange account, and can connect to customer-authorized CRM platforms. Learn more about the Sales Development Agent and review deployment guidance

item.title: [planForChange] Copilot Studio - Set up third-party agent connections in conversations
item.description:
We are announcing improvements to the experience of setting up connections in chats with Copilot Studio agents. These improvements will reach general availability by December 31, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Previously, users needed to leave their conversation, go to a separate connection-management experience, complete setup, and then restart their interaction. This feature is introducing a more seamless way for users to connect agents to third-party services. When an agent requires a connection, users will be guided through a focused setup experience without leaving the conversation or being redirected to the full connection-management portal. When possible, the agent will reuse an existing valid connection.

With this update:
  • Users can establish a required third-party connection from their agent conversation.
  • Users complete only the setup required for the service they are using.
  • Users return directly to the conversation after connecting.
  • An eligible existing connection can be reused instead of configuring another connection.
  • Users can continue working with connected agents across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat.
  • Existing organizational controls that govern which connectors and connections users can access will continue to determine availability.
Please note that developers of agents published through a custom web UI using the Standard harness will be required to make changes to support the new connection experience.

What action do I need to take?
To prepare for this change, we recommend that you:
  • Inform support teams and agent users about the improved connection experience.
  • Review your existing organizational controls for connectors and connections.
For agents published through a custom web UI using the Standard harness, update your implementation to:
  • Open the new connection window.
  • Continue the conversation after connection setup succeeds.
If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Support connection setup in a custom canvas.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: Filter responses by content source
item.description:
[What and why]

We're introducing content source filters in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. This feature allows users to scope a prompt to specific content sources so that Copilot grounds its response only in the sources they select. This helps users focus responses on the most relevant Microsoft 365 content, as well as connected or available third-party sources, while maintaining existing permission and access controls.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat

What will happen

  • Users will see a source selection control in the Copilot Chat prompt area.
  • Users can select one or more available content sources to limit retrieval and grounding for a specific prompt to those sources.
  • Available sources reflect the content sources enabled in your tenant, including Graph connectors and federated connectors available to users.
  • This feature changes where Copilot retrieves information for a prompt and does not change what content a user is permitted to access. Data access, compliance boundaries, and tenant data handling remain unchanged.
  • If no source is selected, Copilot Chat behavior remains unchanged and will use its default orchestration across available sources.
  • Responses will continue to include citations that reflect the selected sources.
  • Source selection applies only to the current prompt and does not persist across sessions.
  • This feature is enabled by default for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Copilot source selection

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Review the display names of published Graph connectors, ensuring that they are clear and recognizable, as these names will appear in the source selection experience for users.
  • Verify the health and search permissions of connectors that should be available to users. Connectors in an error or unpublished state will not appear.

[Learn more]

  • Control and review sources of Microsoft Copilot Chat's responses | Microsoft Support

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Malicious QR code detection in messages
item.description:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is extending malicious URL protection to provide near-real-time detection of malicious destinations embedded in QR codes shared in messages. Teams will analyze QR code destinations to identify potential phishing and fraud threats and display an additional warning when malicious content is detected.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use Microsoft Teams messaging

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams chats, meeting chats, and channels

What will happen

  • Teams will decode and evaluate QR code destinations in inline images shared in 1:1 chats, group chats, meeting chats, and channels.
  • Detection applies to internal and external communications.
  • Images containing QR codes from external senders are already blurred by default. When Teams identifies a malicious QR code, users will also see the warning, “This message contains a link that might be harmful,” and a “Learn about file and link safety” link.
  • QR code images from internal senders are not blurred by default. The same warning will appear when Teams detects a malicious QR code.
  • For users on Teams mobile in China, QR code images are blurred by default regardless of whether the sender is internal or external, and any messages containing malicious QR code will be blocked.
  • Malicious QR code detection is managed by the existing Malicious URL protection setting.
  • The setting is enabled by default. Organizations with Malicious URL protection enabled will automatically receive malicious QR code detection as the feature rolls out.
  • No separate configuration is available or required for malicious QR code detection.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Admins can review or change the existing Malicious URL protection setting in Teams admin center > Settings and policies > Messaging Safety.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users and help desk staff about the additional warning for detected malicious QR codes.
  • Clarify that QR code blurring is a separate precautionary experience and does not mean that Teams has identified a QR code as malicious.
  • Review internal documentation about Teams messaging security and update it if necessary.

Learn more

(Both to be updated closer to rollout.)

  • Malicious URL protection in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [planForChange] Discover usage-based billing (UBB) experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot
item.description:
[What and why:]

As previously announced in MC1479277, we are making usage-based experiences in the Microsoft Copilot app easier to discover. Usage-based billing experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot, will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, even if their organization has not enabled access. Users without an applicable spending policy will see an option to request access or learn more, based on their organization's settings.

Based on customer feedback, we are extending the rollout timeline and introducing an additional admin control that will allow organizations to provide custom guidance to users. These changes give administrators more time to prepare and greater flexibility to manage how users discover and request access to usage-based experiences.

[Rollout schedule:]

The updated rollout schedule is as follows:

  • Mid-November 2026: The new admin setting, "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences," will become available for administrators to configure.
  • Mid-December 2026: An additional option will be introduced to the admin setting, allowing administrators to provide a custom URL as part of the Learn more informational experience that directs users to their own organization’s guidance. The option will be available if you select "Specific users" or “No users” in the setting.
  • End of January 2027: The new discoverability behavior and admin setting will be enforced. The old setting "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing" will be retired. This will apply to customers on deferred release at the end of February 2027.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: 

  • Organizations with users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Platforms/services: 

  • Microsoft Copilot app and Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • Entry points for Cowork, Code, and Autopilot will be visible by default to licensed users starting at the end of January 2027.
  • Users without an applicable spending policy giving them access to the feature will see an informational experience with an option to "Request access" or "Learn more," depending on their how their organization has configured the new "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences" admin setting.
  • Administrators can configure which users are eligible to request access, including the option to prevent access requests.
  • Administrators will be able to provide a custom URL directing users to organizational guidance. Only users who cannot request access will see the secondary URL, "Your organization’s guidance", as part of the Learn more informational experience.  
  • The existing setting, "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing," will continue to apply until it is retired at the end of January 2027.

Examples of the customizable “Your organization’s guidance” link on the informational experience for Cowork and Code. UI subject to change.

This change does not automatically enable usage-based experiences or initiate billing. Users must have an applicable spending policy and available Copilot Credits before they can use these experiences.

[Action required / recommendations:]

We recommend that administrators:

  1. Review the new setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings > Access requests to usage-based billing experiences when it becomes available in mid-November. Starting mid-December, you will be able to configure a custom URL in this setting for users who you decide cannot request access.
  2. Configure access request preferences to determine which users can request access to usage-based experiences.
  3. Prepare organizational guidance and, beginning in mid-December, configure a custom URL if you want to direct users to information specific to your organization.
  4. Review spending policies to ensure that access to usage-based experiences aligns with your organization's requirements.

We recommend reviewing and configuring these settings before the new discoverability behavior is enforced at the end of January 2027.

Learn more: Access requests to usage-based billing experiences (This will be updated in mid-Dec to reflect instructions for the custom URL once available in the setting)

[Compliance considerations:]

This update introduces additional administrative controls for managing access requests and organizational guidance. It does not automatically grant users access to usage-based experiences or change existing spending policy requirements.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Simplifying AI access: Introducing usage-based billing
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the rollout scope and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

The new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business combines everyday AI through a user subscription license with Advanced AI through usage-based billing. Beginning in mid-November, 2026, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants. This phased approach makes it easier for new customers to access eligible usage-based AI experiences, including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities, while reducing billing complexity and preserving flexibility to expand usage over time based on business needs. 

This change will not apply to your existing Microsoft 365 tenant as part of the November rollout. We will share additional information before making usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants. If you’d like to get started sooner, you can enable usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

What is changing 

  • Eligible purchases made by new tenants: Beginning in mid-November, pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business and Microsoft 365 Business with Copilot purchases made by new tenants. 
  • If the new tenant does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy, they will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup. 
  • The resulting spending policy will have a spending limit of 4,000 Copilot credits per user per month, with charges based on actual usage. 
  • Charges apply only when these experiences are used, subject to the usage controls and spending limits established by the administrator. 
  • We will begin rolling out this change to eligible customers in supported markets. The change will not initially be available in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, the Netherlands, Poland, or Spain. We plan to include these markets in the next phase of the rollout in early 2027, with additional details and timing to be shared closer to launch. 

What is not changing 

  • Your existing Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscription benefits and payment terms do not change.
  • Usage-based billing will not be configured by default for your existing tenant as part of the November rollout. 
  • If your organization already has a spending policy configured, the existing spending policy remains in place. 

When this will happen 

  • Mid-November 2026: Usage-based billing default-on will begin for eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants directly from Microsoft, including through Microsoft web. 
  • Existing tenants: We plan to make usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants across all markets beginning in early 2027. We’ll share more details, including specific timing and what to expect, closer to launch. 
  • Optional action: Existing tenants can turn on usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Starting in early 2027: The change applies to eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made through Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) channels, with specific timing to be shared closer to launch. 

How usage-based billing works 

  • When usage-based billing is configured, the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy support access to eligible usage-based experiences. 
  • If you want to turn on usage-based billing for your existing tenant, you can create and manage a spending policy through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Your organization can adjust its spending policies and controls to align with its needs. Disabling usage-based billing prevents access to experiences that require it. 

What you can do to prepare 

  • Review which eligible usage-based experiences—including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities—may support your organization’s needs. 
  • Review your organization’s usage-based billing, governance, and cost-management requirements. 
  • If you choose to turn on usage-based billing ahead of this update, you can create or adjust usage controls and spending policies in Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

Learn more 

  • Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center: https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/copilot/costmanagement/overview 
  • Usage-based billing and cost management for Copilot Credits: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits 
  • Cloud Based Billing: What is a cloud subscription? - Microsoft Cost Management | Microsoft Learn

item.description:

Platforms and services

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Began in late August 2026 and is expected to complete by end of December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action may be required.

Before rollout:

  • Review Microsoft Agent 365 agents available in the All agents page of the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.
  • Review connected agents associated with declarative agents from the Connected agents tab before approving their use.
  • Update any internal governance, agent approval, or deployment processes as appropriate.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance considerationAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This update introduces support for Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents within declarative agents. Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with declarative agents that are connected to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling new AI-powered experiences and workflows.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can install, review, and approve Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center before they are available for use.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Legal plugins in Word and Cowork
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft 365 Copilot is introducing legal plugins in Word and Cowork. These plugins provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents. They can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources, helping legal professionals complete legal work in the Microsoft 365 experiences they already use.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout began in late April 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot commercial licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Word desktop
  • Cowork

What will happen

  • Legal plugins in Copilot provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
  • The plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources.
  • The legal capabilities include more than 20 purpose-built legal skills.
  • In Word desktop, the legal plugin is enabled by default. When enabled, Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks in Word.
  • In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks.
  • The legal skills can help users review contracts against playbooks, draft contracts using templates and precedent agreements, compare contracts with precedents, templates, and policies, and explain tracked changes.
  • The Legal Agent is being retired. Existing Legal Agent users will lose access to the product.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin setup is required.

If your organization plans to use the legal plugins:

  • Ensure Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are assigned to eligible users.
  • Review internal legal workflows that may benefit from these capabilities.
  • Communicate these capabilities to your legal teams.
  • Update internal documentation or help desk guidance as appropriate.
  • Instruct legal team users to add the legal plugin in Cowork.
  • Instruct legal team users to use legal skills in Copilot in Word desktop.

If your organization does not plan to use the legal plugins:

  • Turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center to disable the legal plugin in Word for all users.
  • Turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center to disable the plugin in Cowork for all users.

Learn more

  • Manage Copilot for legal - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. The legal plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 to support legal tasks. The supplied source does not specify changes to data storage or caching.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Legal capabilities previously released as the Legal Agent are being made available as legal plugins in Word and Cowork. They provide purpose-built legal skills and can use work context from Microsoft 365.
Does the change provide users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can use purpose-built legal skills in Copilot in Word and Cowork to summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
Does the change add integration with third-party software products?Yes. The legal plugins can connect to supported third-party legal sources. The supplied sources do not identify specific third-party products.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins can turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The supplied source does not specify whether these controls support Entra ID group membership.
Does the change allow a user to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before using its legal skills. The supplied source does not state that users can independently disable the Word legal plugin.
